assumptions: the substrate executed the check as written (ASM-SUBSTRATE-INTEGRITY)
attrs.evidence: INV-R9.3 checked that a target record IS its declared transformation and let the author declare which fields counted as target-local. GPT-5.6 added `prior_art` to target_local_fields, replaced that field with unrelated text, and ran the full hard gate with every material and the canonical predecessor available: 23 mutations refused, PASS, exit 0. A PRIVILEGE SET A RECORD GRANTS ITSELF IS NOT A CONTRACT. target_local_fields is now the closed triple last_verified / imported_from / readjudicated; TRANSFORM_KINDS declares `forward` (annotates nothing) and `forward_with_historical_evidence_annotation` (annotates exactly `evidence`, for the as-of scoping of a historical count). Both attacks are registered: MUT-TRANSFORM-LOCAL-WIDENED and MUT-TRANSFORM-ANNOTATION-WIDENED, the second using a plausible `why` so the reason field cannot carry the widening either.

coverage.domain: the closed target-local set and the per-kind annotation sets
coverage.enumerator: TARGET_LOCAL_FIELDS and TRANSFORM_KINDS, against which every declared field is resolved

evidence_qualifiers.population: every field of every forwarded target record

attrs.gap: THE VOCABULARY IS SMALL BECAUSE THE INSTANCE IS SMALL. One transform kind beyond plain forwarding, one annotatable field, eight production records. A future integration wanting a different legitimate annotation must add a kind here and a mutation beside it — which is the intended cost, and it is a cost, not a proof that the two kinds are sufficient.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6’s INV-R9.3 audit §6. Same shape as INV-R9.2’s closed disposition vocabulary one layer in: there the bucket NAMES were author-expandable, here the FIELD PRIVILEGES were.
attrs.review_focus: Two kinds and one annotatable field. Is that a vocabulary or a pair of special cases?
attrs.statement: The fields a forwarded target record may differ in are fixed by a vocabulary, not by the record: target-local metadata is a closed set, and each transform kind names exactly which semantic field it may annotate.
